stories.title: Kenya: MPs to Consider Six Bills Seeking Sweeping Reforms in Education Sector
stories.summary: Kenya: MPs to Consider Six Bills Seeking Sweeping Reforms in Education Sector 12 August 2026 Capital FM (Nairobi) By Irene Mwangi Nairobi — The National Assembly is set to consider six Bills proposing far-reaching reforms across Kenya's education sector, with the proposed legislation targeting basic education governance, national assessments, curriculum development, teacher training, tertiary education funding and the recognition of academic and professional qualifications. The Bills, sponsored by Leader of the Majority Party Kimani Ichung'wah, have been introduced in the House as the government seeks to establish new legal frameworks for the implementation and management of the education system. The six pieces of legislation are the Tertiary Education Placement and Funding Bill, 2026; Basic Education Bill, 2026; Kenya National Educational Assessments Council Bill, 2026; Pre-Service Education and In-Service Training Bill, 2026; Kenya National Qualifications Framework (Amendment) Bill, 2026; and Kenya Institute of Curriculum Development (Amendment) Bill, 2026. The Bills have been committed to the National Assembly's Education Committee for consideration and public participation.The Basic Education Bill, 2026, seeks to overhaul the legal framework governing basic education, including the administration and governance of learning institutions, quality assurance and standards, special needs education and the management of education information. stories.title: Africa: A Century of Agricultural Investment in Sudan - Why Has Development Failed?
stories.summary: Africa: A Century of Agricultural Investment in Sudan - Why Has Development Failed? 11 August 2026 African Arguments opinion By Hassan Ali Sanhori This article is translated and adapted from an Arabic article published in Sudanese Online . The ideas reflect arguments presented by the author in his book on agriculture in Sudan. For decades, Sudan has been described as one of Africa's countries with the greatest agricultural potential. Its vast arable land, diverse climatic zones, water resources, and livestock wealth have repeatedly led policymakers to portray it as a potential "breadbasket" for Africa and the Arab world. Kenyan immigration officers stopped him at the gate. According to multiple reports, his Kenyan passport had been fraudulently obtained. The current Ebola outbreak caused by the Bundibugyo species, was declared by DRC health officials on 15 May and declared a public health emergency of international concern by the World Health Organization ( WHO ) two days later. With more than 4,000 confirmed cases, it is both the second-largest and the fastest-growing on record . Only West Africa's 2014 to 2016 outbreak, which saw more than 11,000 deaths, was larger. Just three months into this Ebola emergency, the death toll is already close to the total number of people killed in the 2018 to 2020 epidemic, which saw fewer overall cases.

stories.title: Africa: As Funding Shrinks, Africa's SRHR Movement Vows Not to Retreat
stories.summary: Africa: As Funding Shrinks, Africa's SRHR Movement Vows Not to Retreat Sonke Gender Justice/Supplied Across Africa, countless people face significant barriers to essential sexual and reproductive healthcare, often experiencing violence, shame, and coercion. 12 August 2026 allAfrica.com By Melody Chironda Mombasa, Kenya — As funding shrinks, civic space narrows and opposition to sexual and reproductive rights grows across Africa, advocates are gathering in Mombasa with a simple message: progress cannot be taken for granted. More than 250 advocates, policymakers, youth leaders, healthcare providers, researchers, civil society organisations and community leaders from across the continent have converged for the MenEngage Africa SRHR Learning and Exchange Symposium, PROGRESS 2026, a three-day gathering focused on defending bodily autonomy, advancing sexual and reproductive justice and finding new ways to push forward in the face of growing resistance. The symposium, organised by Sonke Gender Justice and MenEngage Africa held under the theme Reclaiming Autonomy, Advancing Sexual and Reproductive Justice in the Face of Resistance, and comes at a critical moment for the region's SRHR movement. Activists across the continent are confronting shrinking civic space, rising opposition to SRHR, patchy delivery of Comprehensive Sexuality Education, and persistent barriers facing adolescents, women, persons with disabilities, LGBTQIA+ persons, and other marginalised groups. These challenges are compounded further by conservative policy shifts, climate-related crises , and the growing threat of technology-facilitated gender-based violence.

stories.summary: Nigeria and Mozambique Show How Health Systems Can Withstand Funding Cuts black.illustrations (file image) 12 August 2026 allAfrica.com By Melody Chironda For decades, many health programmes across sub-Saharan Africa have relied on a familiar model: donors fund disease-specific projects, parallel delivery structures are built around them, and services expand or contract with the funding cycle. That model is now under pressure. As bilateral aid shrinks, countries that have relied heavily on external financing are confronting the vulnerabilities created by fragmented systems. But experiences in Nigeria and Mozambique suggest that resilience may not always require replacing every dollar lost. In some cases, it may begin with changing how existing resources are organised.

Harmon President Joseph Nyuma Boakai has made perhaps his most consequential national security appointment since assuming office, naming former Defense Minister, retired Major General Daniel Dee Ziankahn, as Director General of the Liberia Drug Enforcement Agency (LDEA) in a move that signals a fundamental shift in the government's strategy against transnational narcotics trafficking. The appointment comes at a defining moment for Liberia's anti-drug campaign -- one marked by record cocaine seizures, allegations of institutional infiltration by organized crime, dismissals of senior security officials, and mounting international scrutiny over whether Liberia has become an emerging transit and storage hub for global narcotics syndicates. Rather than selecting another career drug enforcement officer, President Boakai has entrusted the agency to one of the country's most experienced military minds, suggesting that the administration increasingly views narcotics trafficking not merely as a law enforcement problem but as a national security emergency. Ziankahn's appointment follows months of extraordinary anti-narcotics operations that have transformed Liberia's security landscape.

stories.title: Zambie: dans la région de la Copperbelt, l’extraction de cuivre entraîne une pollution massive et pas de retombées économiques
stories.summary: Zambie: dans la région de la Copperbelt, l’extraction de cuivre entraîne une pollution massive et pas de retombées économiques À quelques jours de l’élection présidentielle en Zambie, le 14 août prochain, le président sortant et candidat Hakainde Hichilema promet de tripler la production de cuivre pour renflouer les caisses de l’État, déclaré en faillite en 2021. Mais les habitants de la province de la Copperbelt (la ceinture de cuivre), au nord du pays, ne voient aucun développement économique à l’exploitation de l’immense réserve du minerai essentiel pour les batteries électriques, notamment : pis, ils subissent les multiples pollutions liées à l’extraction minière. Publié le : 11/08/2026 - 07:39 2 min Temps de lecture Exploitation d'une mine de cuivre à ciel ouvert, en Zambie. © mabus13 / Getty Images Par : RFI Publicité Lire la suite La région est stratégique pour toutes les grandes puissances mondiales : Chine , États-Unis , Royaume-Uni , Suisse , Inde , et autres souhaitent accaparer ces minerais et la Zambie espère tirer profit de ces ressources pour sortir de son endettement évalué à environ 30 milliards de dollars en 2024. Mais la population voit les choses d’un autre œil. « C’est ici à Chingola que la pollution des mines est la plus importante. Je crois que c’est le pire endroit de Zambie tant la pollution est répandue » : Eugène Mulanga de la fondation Caritas Zambie est dépité.

stories.title: Au Maroc, la fin du démarchage téléphonique vers la France menace plus de 40 000 emplois
stories.summary: Une loi adoptée en France interdit toute prospection sans accord explicite du client à partir du 11 août. Elle met en danger des dizaines de milliers de salariés dans les centres d’appels marocains, largement dépendants du marché hexagonal.

stories.title: RDC: Kinshasa défend son milliard de dollars issu d'eurobonds pour des grands projets
stories.summary: RDC: Kinshasa défend son milliard de dollars issu d'eurobonds pour des grands projets En République démocratique du Congo, l’eurobond de 1,25 milliard de dollars très attendu sur de gros projets. Quatre mois après son émission avec succès, une question s’impose : fallait-il mobiliser d’un seul coup l’intégralité de cette dette, alors qu’une partie des fonds n’est pas encore utilisée ? Un député du parti présidentiel met en garde contre un coût financier jugé prématuré. Une lecture que le ministère des Finances rejette fermement. Pour lui, un eurobond inaugural obéit à une logique bien plus large que celle d’une simple ligne de crédit.

stories.title: A burial row over Zambia's late president has turned its election into a hot contest
stories.summary: Image source, AFP via Getty Images Image caption, More than eight million registered voters have 14 presidential candidates to choose from By Dingindaba Buyoya BBC Focus on Africa ,Â Reporting from Lusaka Published 11 August 2026 A spectre is hanging over the Zambian election campaign in the shape of former President Edgar Lungu. Despite having died more than a year ago in South Africa, his body remains unburied amid a bitter dispute between President Hakainde Hichilema and the Lungu family that has sharpened political divisions. This has had a role in energising support for the opposition National Reconciliation Party for Unity and Prosperity (NRPUP), particularly in the northern half of the country, traditional strongholds of Lungu's Patriotic Front (PF), as people see it as offering the best chance to unseat the incumbent. Meanwhile, it has complicated the second-term bid of Hichilema and his United Party for National Development (UPND), which draws its core support from the south, west and north-west while seeking to expand its reach nationwide. The political battle is playing out on the streets of the capital, Lusaka.

stories.title: « Ebola se propage à une vitesse que nous n’avions encore jamais observée » : l’alerte de Jean-Jacques Muyembe, codécouvreur du virus
stories.summary: Le virologue congolais, qui a mis au jour le virus en 1976, revient, dans un entretien au « Monde », sur l’actuelle propagation de l’épidémie due à Ebola en République démocratique du Congo. En seulement trois mois, le nombre de morts s’approche du bilan humain de l’épidémie de 2018, qui avait duré vingt-deux mois.

stories.title: Migrant Crisis Reveals Vast Differences Between Ceuta and Its Moroccan Neighbor
stories.summary: Ceuta, Spain, and Fnideq, Morocco, are physically separated by only a mile, but they are intertwined by family and trade. A recent border crisis is the latest chapter in their story.

stories.title: Vers la fin du roi dollar en Afrique ?
stories.summary: La domination de la devise américaine sur l’économie mondiale commence à montrer des signes d’essoufflement. Quelles conséquentes ce phénomène peut-il avoir sur les pays africains ?

stories.title: Tchad : Succès Masra, un an de prison et de négociations secrètes avec Mahamat Idriss Déby Itno
stories.summary: Tchad : Succès Masra, un an de prison et de négociations secrètes avec Mahamat Idriss Déby Itno Un an après sa condamnation, l’opposant tchadien Succès Masra reste en prison. stories.title: Jean Kaseya : « L’épidémie d’Ebola en RDC n’est pas sous contrôle et son extension n’est pas contenue »
stories.summary: Alors que l’épidémie d’Ebola poursuit sa progression en RDC, Jean Kaseya, le directeur général d’Africa CDC, le Centre africain de contrôle et de prévention des maladies, dresse un bilan sans concession de la riposte.

stories.title: We are chasing Ebola virus - it is ahead of us, WHO warns
stories.summary: Image source, Reuters Image caption, Health workers need to be fully protected as the virus can spread from touching bodily fluids. By Damian Zane Published 10 August 2026 The latest Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo began at least three months before it was officially declared - meaning the health authorities are still playing catch-up, the World Health Organization (WHO) has warned. More than 1,900 people have died from the virus since that declaration on 15 May, making this the second-worst Ebola outbreak ever. Infection rates are still high, adding to the concern that the authorities are struggling to get to grips with the spread of the disease. The epicentre of this outbreak of the Bundibugyo species of Ebola, is in the east of DR Congo where insecurity has hampered control efforts.

stories.title: Au Cameroun, les producteurs de cacao en quête de jours meilleurs
stories.summary: Au Cameroun, les producteurs de cacao en quête de jours meilleurs La production, la transformation locale et les exportations ont toutes été orientées à la baisse au terme de la dernière campagne. En cause, la décision de la majorité des 400 000 cultivateurs de conserver leurs stocks, dans l’espoir d’une remontée des cours. Dans une plantation familiale de cacao à Ebebda, au Cameroun, le 30 novembre 2024. © Daniel BELOUMOU OLOMO / AFP Par Omer Mbadi (à Yaoundé) Publié le 10 août à 17h01 Lecture : 3 minutes. Ils n’ont réussi qu’à commercialiser 125 468 tonnes lors de la campagne cacaoyère 2025-2026 qui s’est achevée à la mi-juillet, soit une baisse de 66 544 tonnes (- 35 %) par rapport à la campagne précédente.

stories.title: Les étudiants marocains touchés de plein fouet par la hausse des frais d’inscription en France
stories.summary: Un décret, pris le 19 mai, restreint les possibilités d’exonération des droits d’inscription différenciés pour les étudiants non européens. Parmi eux, les Marocains sont les plus nombreux à étudier dans les facultés françaises.

stories.title: La Guinée demande à la France la restitution du crâne de Bokar Biro, résistant à la colonisation française
stories.summary: Conakry entend récupérer les crânes du dernier souverain de l’Etat théocratique du Fouta-Djallon et de trois de ses proches, près de cent trente ans après leur assassinat par les troupes coloniales françaises.

stories.title: How climate change is reshaping Africa's malaria risk
stories.summary: https://p.dw.com/p/5IYdD Malaria spreads most efficiently at around 25°C (77°F) Image: RealityImages/Zoonar/picture alliance Advertisement For decades, global efforts towards the eradication of malaria , especially in sub-Saharan Africa, have focused essentially on West and Central Africa, where the disease is most endemic. The WHO African Region accounts for about 95% of global malaria cases and deaths. Nearly half of all malaria deaths in the region occur in Nigeria (31.9%), the Democratic Republic of Congo (11.7%) and Niger (6.1%). Children under 5 years of age account for about 76% of malaria deaths in the region. To stem the tide of malaria cases across Africa, the global health body has recommended a wider use of the RTS,S/AS01 malaria vaccine among children living in regions with moderate to high malaria transmission by the Plasmodium falciparum — a parasite that causes 95% of all malaria infections in Africa .

stories.title: Pétrole : « L’Afrique reste vulnérable à l’instabilité des coûts d’importation »
stories.summary: Kamel Koné, entrepreneur et président du lobby ivoirien du pétrole et du gaz, appelle à un sursaut panafricain pour la structuration d’un « écosystème énergétique plus résilient sur le long terme », à même de résister à des crises comme celle en cours dans le détroit d’Ormuz.

stories.title: Cameroun : entre Oswald Baboke et Ferdinand Ngoh Ngoh, le conflit que la présidence veut cacher
stories.summary: Longtemps au-dessus de la mêlée, Oswald Baboke se retrouve au cœur d’un affrontement avec le tout-puissant secrétaire général de la présidence, Ferdinand Ngoh Ngoh. Faux décrets, trafic d’or, course à la vice-présidence : récit d’une guerre qui embrase le palais.

stories.title: L’activiste guinéen Bella Bah porté disparu après son interpellation dans une école
stories.summary: Selon le mouvement citoyen Tournons La Page-Guinée, l’enseignant a été interpellé à Conakry ce samedi 8 août par « des hommes en tenue de la gendarmerie nationale, cagoulés, dans l’enceinte de sa propre école ». Sa disparition intervient quelques heures après une prise de position controversée visant un imam.

stories.title: Au Sénégal, Petrosen en campagne pour reconquérir les investisseurs
stories.summary: Sitôt installé à la tête de la Société nationale des pétroles du Sénégal, Thierno Seydou Ly place la reconquête des investisseurs au cœur de sa feuille de route pour relancer les projets majeurs.

stories.title: Algérie-Mali : qui est Kamel Retieb, l’ambassadeur dont Alger autorise le retour à Bamako ?
stories.summary: Algérie-Mali : qui est Kamel Retieb, l’ambassadeur dont Alger autorise le retour à Bamako ? Quinze mois après son rappel en pleine crise diplomatique, en avril 2025, l’ambassadeur d’Algérie a regagné Bamako. L’ambassadeur algérien Kamel Retieb, reçu par Abdoulaye Diop, le ministre malien des Affaires étrangères, à Bamako, le 20 juillet 2026. © Bureau de l’Information et de la Presse/MAECI Par Arezki Said Publié le 10 août à 08h04, modifié à 09h21 Lecture : 4 minutes. stories.title: Ancestral Visions of the Future review – visceral cine-memoir is a haunting return to Lesotho
stories.summary: Ecstatic and pained mysticism … Ancestral Visions of the Future. Photograph: Agat Films View image in fullscreen Ecstatic and pained mysticism … Ancestral Visions of the Future. Photograph: Agat Films Review Ancestral Visions of the Future review – visceral cine-memoir is a haunting return to Lesotho Lemohang Jeremiah Mosese pairs his literary-grade voiceover with propulsive, prophetic images to interrogate his identity and that of his colonialism-carved homeland H ere is a captivating stream of consciousness film about exile, roots and identity by Lemohang Jeremiah Mosese, director of the lauded 2019 activism story This Is Not a Burial, It’s a Resurrection . It’s ostensibly a cine-memoir looking back from the vantage point of present-day Berlin to his upbringing in Lesotho, narrated by Mosese’s dense, literary-grade voiceover. But there’s something propulsive and prophetic about the accompanying hyper-vivid images from rural and urban life.

stories.title: Comment Alpha Condé tente de renaître sur les rives du fleuve Congo
stories.summary: Depuis Brazzaville, où il séjourne à l’invitation de Denis Sassou Nguesso, Alpha Condé tente de retrouver une influence panafricaine. L’ex-président multiplie les initiatives, mais garde en tête un objectif principal : rentrer en Guinée.

stories.title: « Bolle Jos », le « parrain » de la cocaïne qui aurait fait de la Sierra Leone un narco-État
stories.summary: Vu aux côtés du président Julius Maada Bio lors d’un office du Nouvel an, le trafiquant néerlandais Jos Leijdekkers plonge la Sierra Leone dans une crise politique et diplomatique sans précédent.

stories.title: Evidence that South African special forces murdered top detective shared with BBC
stories.summary: Image source, Mathipa family Image caption, Lt Col Frans Mathipa was a respected detective and father of five By Yeshiel Panchia ,Â Dino Mahtani Â and Â Nick Norman-Butler ,Â BBC Eye Investigations Published 10 August 2026 Senior police detective Frans Mathipa had been fighting for four months to gain access to a crucial piece of information in the case he was working on. Finally, he was told, it was going to come his way. But he feared his pursuit of it could cost him his life. Two days later, his car was found overturned - he had been shot dead while driving. Now seven members of South Africa's special forces, and one military police officer, have been charged with murdering Lt Col Mathipa, a highly respected officer, in August 2023.

stories.title: Mali : au moins 10 militaires tués dans l’attaque d’une caserne dans le centre du pays
stories.summary: Le Jnim a revendiqué l’attaque menée dimanche 9 août contre une caserne de l’armée malienne dans la ville de San, dans la région de Ségou. L’armée affirme que « la situation est sous contrôle ».

stories.title: Le pape Léon XIV appelle à l’ouverture de couloirs humanitaires au Soudan
stories.summary: « J’exhorte la communauté internationale à soutenir les efforts visant à instaurer un cessez-le-feu immédiat », a déclaré le souverain pontife, au sujet d’un conflit qui a fait des dizaines de milliers de morts et déplacé des millions de personnes.

stories.title: Au Sénégal, le long combat des héritiers d’El-Hadj Omar Tall pour le retour du « trésor de Ségou » pillé sous la colonisation
stories.summary: Le guide spirituel soufi, dont les disciples se comptent par centaines de milliers, était un érudit et un combattant anticolonialiste du XIXᵉ siècle. stories.title: Nigeria's mass wedding - and how telling lovers from fraudsters is proving tricky
stories.summary: Image source, Getty Images Image caption, All the new wedding outfits are paid for by the Kano state government By Mansur Abubakar Reporting from Abuja Published 9 August 2026 Celebrations have turned the northern Nigerian city of Kano into a riot of colour and excitement over the last week as 1,500 couples married at a mass wedding. For days the city's streets have been buzzing with bridal parties and their families preparing outfits and attending other organised events. On Friday, brides in red hijabs with grooms in matching red hats and white robes went to the palace of the Emir, the city's traditional Muslim leader, for the main ceremony where they officially became husband and wife. The nuptials culminated on Saturday with a wedding breakfast hosted by Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf, who offered his blessing to the newlyweds. The Kano state government sponsored this initiative, spending 1.5bn naira ($1m; Â£815,000) to support those tying the knot - providing the bride's dowry and furniture for the couple's first home.

stories.title: Carlos Echeverria Jesus, politiste : « La crise de Ceuta traduit les ambitions territoriales du Maroc »
stories.summary: Après que 72 000 migrants venus de la ville marocaine de Fnideq ont atteint l’enclave espagnole de Ceuta les 30 et 31 juillet, le directeur de l’Observatoire de Ceuta et Melilla analyse, dans un entretien au « Monde », l’état des relations entre le royaume chérifien et son voisin espagnol.

stories.title: ‘We have no tents or blankets’: Ceuta migrants struggle to survive brutal heat and freezing nights
stories.summary: A woman from Morocco and other migrants wait and sleep in the open in Ceuta, Spain, on Thursday. Photograph: Violeta Santos Moura/Reuters View image in fullscreen A woman from Morocco and other migrants wait and sleep in the open in Ceuta, Spain, on Thursday. Photograph: Violeta Santos Moura/Reuters ‘We have no tents or blankets’: Ceuta migrants struggle to survive brutal heat and freezing nights Authorities wrestle with fallout from mass border crossing, as tense Spanish enclave fears it will happen again Along the wide avenues and tree-lined plazas of Ceuta’s centre, there were few hints of the recent events that catapulted the Spanish enclave on the north African coast into global headlines. But less than a mile away from the bustling bars and restaurants, at the nearby El Trampolín beach, the lingering impact was impossible to ignore. “We’re sleeping here on the beach, out in the open, without tents or blankets,” said Imad, 26, one of several thousand people believed to be still in Ceuta after last week’s extraordinary influx of more than 72,000 migrants into the Spanish territory on the edge of Morocco . “We don’t have bathrooms,” added the Yemen national. “I barely manage two hours of sleep, as it’s incredibly cold by the sea at night, and during the day the heat is unbearable.” View image in fullscreen A man prays inside a makeshift mosque marked out with stones on El Trampolín beach in Ceuta, where hundreds of migrants have been sheltering. Photograph: Okba Mohammad One week on, while questions continue to swirl over what exactly prompted the incident, the city’s shops and markets have reopened and many of the 84,000 residents have resumed their daily routines.

stories.title: Their African Islands Were Set to Be Decolonized. Then the U.S. Bombed Iran.
stories.summary: The inhabitants of the Chagos Islands were expelled by the British 60 years ago. Refugees were anxious to return this year, but their hopes have been caught in a morass of geopolitics.

stories.title: Les arrestations en Algérie de Mehdi Laribi et Djamel Djeha, deux cadres présumés du narcotrafic, signe du timide réchauffement entre Paris et Alger
stories.summary: Le ministre de la justice, Gérald Darmanin, s’est félicité, jeudi 6 août, de cette « coopération relancée au service de la sécurité de nos deux pays ». stories.title: Spain to introduce temporary border checks on visitors from Italy
stories.summary: The checks, which come ‘amid the persistent irregular migration pressure’ facing Italy, will starts at midnight on Saturday. Photograph: Antonio Sempere/AP View image in fullscreen The checks, which come ‘amid the persistent irregular migration pressure’ facing Italy, will starts at midnight on Saturday. Photograph: Antonio Sempere/AP Spain to introduce temporary border checks on visitors from Italy Move comes in response to Rome imposing similar measures after mass migration rush to Ceuta Spain has announced it will introduce temporary border checks on visitors from Italy in response to Rome imposing similar measures after a mass rush of people from Morocco into Ceuta. The checks, which come “amid the persistent irregular migration pressure” facing Italy , will start at midnight on Saturday and last until 7 September, Spain’s interior ministry said in a statement. Hours earlier, Spain threatened Italy with countermeasures if it did not swiftly lift its own border checks, drawing a rebuff from Rome.

stories.title: Sudan's invisible children - born in war with no legal identity
stories.summary: Image source, Reuters Image caption, If a mother cannot provide the name of her child's father, she is often unable to get a birth certificate By Ethar Shalaby ,Â BBC News Arabic Â and Â Patricia Whitehorne ,Â BBC Africa Published 7 August 2026 Warning: This story contains details some may find distressing A 17-year-old Sudanese girl holds a young child in her arms with a heavy calm that belies her age and the concerns she has for his future. "This son of mine has no father, no birth certificate and no national number," Amira, whose name has been changed to protect her identity, tells the BBC. Looking down at him, she speaks slowly as if still trying to grasp the details of what has happened to her since the civil war erupted in Sudan. She and her family used to live in the eastern neighbourhoods of el-Fasher, a city that came under siege from the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF), which has been in a brutal power struggle with the military since April 2023. El-Fasher was the army's last stronghold in the western region of Darfur until it fell to the RSF and allied Arab militias after 18 months last October. For the tens of thousands of civilians trapped inside the city, it was a nightmare â with constant bombardment, clashes and suffering from a lack of food.

Photograph: Jospin Mwisha/AFP/Getty Images Ebola virus behind massive outbreak in DRC could be mutating, officials say Cases have passed 4,000 and health watchdog plans to go door to door to find patients in major response escalation The virus causing a massive outbreak of Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo could be mutating, health officials fear, as confirmed cases pass 4,000. Africa’s public health watchdog said the time for incremental action was over as they announced plans to scale up every aspect of the response and go “door to door” looking for patients. The Ebola outbreak, caused by the Bundibugyo strain of the virus, was first reported on 15 May, although there are suspicions the disease could have been spreading since January.

Photograph: Bloomberg/Getty Images US to shut five consulates as critics fear China could fill diplomatic vacuum State department informs Congress of planned closures in Canada, Grenada, Japan, Indonesia and Cameroon The US state department is to shut five foreign consulates and missions across Asia, Africa, North America and the Caribbean , drawing criticism that it is leaving a diplomatic vacuum at risk of being filled by China. The US Congress has been served notice of the impending closures, which are being justified on cost grounds and follow a reassessment of the US’s bilateral relationships with a range of countries since Donald Trump returned to the White House in January 2025. According to a notice served to several congressional committees, missions will close in St George’s, Grenada; Nagoya, Japan; Medan, Indonesia; Douala, Cameroon; and Winnipeg, Canada.

Photograph: Fabrice Coffrini/AFP/Getty Images ‘Morocco feels emboldened’: Trump’s influence in spotlight after Ceuta disaster Washington-Rabat ties under scrutiny as questions swirl over what led to deadly influx into tiny Spanish territory T he cosy relationship between Washington and Rabat has long been flaunted by both sides, from Morocco’s announcement this year that it would be the first African state to join Donald Trump’s Board of Peace to the congratulatory message recently sent by Trump to mark King Mohammed VI’s 27 years in power. The latest example landed this week. As Spain grappled with the aftermath of the sudden influx – and swift return – of more than 70,000 people into Ceuta, Morocco’s monarch confirmed he had named a $1bn highway flanking the disputed territory of Western Sahara after Trump.

stories.title: What's behind the Algeria-Morocco rivalry?
stories.summary: https://p.dw.com/p/5IMUo Some 60,000 migrants crossed into Ceuta from Morocco several days ago Image: Ian Whittaker/News Licensing/IMAGO Advertisement Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez traveled to Algeria on July 20 for talks with Algerian President Abdelmadjid Tebboune and Prime Minister Sifi Ghrieb. The meeting's aim was to resolve a diplomatic row that erupted between both countries in 2022 after Spain sided with Morocco's autonomy proposal to resolve the Western Sahara conflict — much to Algeria's dismay. It is a matter of debate whether Spain's rapprochement with Algeria outraged Morocco so much that it deliberately allowed tens of thousands of migrants to storm the Spanish exclave of Ceuta , even though both countries have improved their relations enormously in recent years. Spanish daily El Pais has certainly entertained the possibility of Moroccan meddling. "Ceuta tensions coincided with Pedro Sanchez's trip to Algeria, a regional rival of the [Moroccan] Alawite Kingdom," an opinion piece in the Spanish paper notes. The article later states that "any attempt to use immigration as a bargaining chip is unacceptable." Moroccan interior ministry spokesperson Rachid El Khalfi has rejected such accusations, saying the incident resulted from "the malicious exploitation of the digital space," as well as "misleading information" and misinterpretations of a recent Spanish Supreme Court ruling on the rights of arriving migrants.

stories.title: Spain’s Pedro Sánchez is a progressive outlier in Europe – and over Ceuta, he is being made to pay for it | Eoghan Gilmartin
stories.summary: Pedro Sánchez speaking in Ceuta, Spain, last week. ‘He called out the ‘prejudice, misinformation and attacks’ of many of his [EU] peers.’ Photograph: Fabian Bimmer/Reuters View image in fullscreen Pedro Sánchez speaking in Ceuta, Spain, last week. ‘He called out the ‘prejudice, misinformation and attacks’ of many of his [EU] peers.’ Photograph: Fabian Bimmer/Reuters Spain’s Pedro Sánchez is a progressive outlier in Europe – and over Ceuta, he is being made to pay for it Eoghan Gilmartin The Spanish PM has been one of few European leaders to stand up to Trump. He now faces coercive diplomacy and an emboldened far right at home T he dramatic footage last Thursday of thousands of migrants entering Spain’s north African enclave of Ceuta generated an online frenzy among the far right. And the alarmist rhetoric was also evident in the European mainstream, as EU leaders wasted little time attributing the chaotic scenes to Spain’s liberal immigration policies. In a letter organised by Italy and Denmark, and signed by 22 EU heads of government, they appeared to blame the crisis on Spanish prime minister Pedro Sánchez’s recent programme to regularise undocumented migrants, which received more than a million applications . They argued that Europe must “[address] all policies that can serve as pull factors”.

stories.title: Fact check: Did misleading claims about Spain's migration law trigger the Ceuta crisis?
stories.summary: https://p.dw.com/p/5IG1B Tens of thousands of people attempted to cross from Morocco into Ceuta during a major migration surge that authorities linked, among other factors, to misleading information circulating online Image: Antonio Sempere/AP Photo/picture alliance Advertisement Misleading social media posts appear to have contributed to a sudden surge in migrant crossings into Spain's North African exclave of Ceuta . Tens of thousands of people attempted to cross from Morocco in late July . According to authorities, dozens drowned or were killed in crowd-related incidents during the crossings, which triggered a major humanitarian crisis. European, Spanish and Moroccan authorities blamed the sudden surge in crossings on incorrect information circulating on social media and human traffickers. A recent Spanish Supreme Court ruling on migrant returns became the focus of many of the misleading claims.

Photograph: Aaron Ufumeli/EPA View image in fullscreen A maize crop affected by lack of rain in Zimbabwe. ‘The biggest food security impact, in southern Africa, will be during the 2027 to 2028 lean season,’ one expert said. Photograph: Aaron Ufumeli/EPA El Niño could push 50m people into acute hunger before end of next year UN forecasters warn of worsening conditions in 45 countries currently experiencing severe food insecurity About 50 million people are likely to be pushed into acute hunger before the end of next year by the rapidly developing El Niño weather system , according to forecasting. This is in addition to the hundreds of millions of people already facing dangerous levels of hunger, owing to years of drought in parts of Africa and pressure on food prices from the war in Iran. Even if the forecast El Niño is less strong than some models predict, it will tip many countries over the edge, adding more than a fifth to the 225 million people in 45 countries currently in acute food insecurity, the UN’s World Food Programme (WFP) warned on Wednesday.
